rationale: sphereflake is a recursive floating-point ray-tracing benchmark (Large, Misc-C++), so the profile is dominated by dense FP/vector arithmetic, deep recursion, and a measured runtime, with sparse external interaction and few callsites/globals per function; SUB is weighted aggressively because algebraic substitution of FP and integer expressions is nearly free in time/size and directly obscures the vector-math inner loops, and SPLIT is kept cheap-and-enabled as a low-risk diversity add-on; FLA and BCF are security-valued but deliberately penalized on RuntimeCost/SizeCost since this benchmark's execution time and code footprint are part of its score and recursion plus FP loops amplify bogus-block overhead, so they should apply only to functions whose features (branchy, non-FP-dominated) favor them; IBR is moderately penalized because indirect branches disrupt the hot recursive traversal yet still add real disassembly resistance; ICALL carries the highest CorrectnessRisk weight since sphereflake has few indirect-call opportunities and forcing them through function pointers risks breaking the FP-heavy call patterns for modest gain; IGV is enabled moderately because hiding global configuration/geometry tables via indirection is cheap and low-risk in this workload.
